keyVerseText: All these were of costly stones, according to the measures of hewed stones, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside toward the great court.
rootMeaning: The root of טֵפַח (ṭêphach) comes from the verb טָפַח (ṭâphach), which conveys the ideas of spreading out, extending, or carrying on the palms of the hand. This root emphasizes a physical action related to the hand, such as flattening or nursing a child, highlighting a sense of measured extension or nurturing. Thus, beyond the common English gloss of 'handbreadth,' the root suggests a deliberate, tangible span defined by the breadth of a hand as an instrument of measurement and care.
usageInScripture: The word טֵפַח is used in Scripture primarily as a unit of measurement equivalent to a handbreadth, appearing four times with consistent translation as a span or width of the hand. It also carries an architectural sense, referring to 'coping,' a structural support element, as seen in 1 Kings 7:9. This range from a simple measure of length to a technical architectural term reveals the word's practical importance in both daily life and sacred construction, underscoring precision and intentionality in biblical description.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding טֵפַח enriches our appreciation for the precision and care with which God’s Word describes His creation and the temple, reflecting divine order and intentionality. The notion of a handbreadth as a unit of measure reminds believers that God’s work is detailed and exact, symbolizing His sovereign control over all things, even the smallest dimensions. The root’s connection to nurturing gestures also invites reflection on God’s tender care for His people, who are measured and known intimately by Him. This word thus bridges the tangible and the spiritual, illustrating how God’s hands both build and sustain.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 7:9, the phrase 'unto the coping' uses טֵפַח to describe the extent of the temple’s foundation and finishing work, emphasizing the careful craftsmanship from the base to the uppermost architectural detail. This word highlights the completeness and precision of the temple’s construction, which points to the holiness and perfection demanded by God. It reminds readers that every part of God’s dwelling, no matter how small, is measured and made with divine purpose and care.
